items.title: Section: Cunda's Question About Ritual Purity, and the Fifth Skilful Understanding Opens

items.zh: 如是已說緣起善巧。處非處善巧我今當說。總嗢拕南曰：體顯現初、門差別後。
items.en: Thus the skilful understanding of dependent origination has been explained. The skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid shall now be explained. The summary verse states: essential nature, manifestation, and the reason for its being taught come first; the fourfold gate of distinctions comes after.

items.title: Section: Defining "Valid" and "Invalid," and Why the Buddha Bothered Teaching the Difference

items.zh: 問：何等為處？答：於彼彼事理無相違。問：何等非處？答：於彼彼事理有相違。是名處非處體。問：何故世尊顯示處非處善巧耶？答：為欲顯示染污、清淨正方便智無失壞故。問：應以幾門觀察處非處耶？答：四。由佛世尊但以四門宣說一切處非處故。何等為四？一、成辦門，二、合會門，三、證得門，四、現行門。問：何緣以此四門說處非處？答：為欲示現遍一切種差別門故。
items.en: Question: what is the valid? Answer: whenever, for a given matter, there is no contradiction with its principle. Question: what is the invalid? Answer: whenever, for a given matter, there is a contradiction with its principle. This is called the essential nature of the valid and the invalid. Question: why does the Blessed One reveal the skilful understanding of the valid and the invalid? Answer: in order to reveal that correct wisdom and skilful means regarding both the defiled and the pure remain undamaged and unimpaired. Question: through how many approaches should the valid and the invalid be observed? Answer: four, since the Blessed One taught the whole of the valid and the invalid using only four approaches. What are the four? First, the gate of accomplishment; second, the gate of combination; third, the gate of attainment; fourth, the gate of active manifestation. Question: for what reason are the valid and the invalid taught through these four approaches? Answer: in order to reveal every distinguishing approach across every category without exception.

items.title: Section: Why the Eye Can Never Hear, and Why Earth Can Never Turn Into Fire

items.zh: 云何一切種差別？謂依初成辦門，彼所不攝餘差別相，我當顯示。當知此差別略說有三種。一、諸根越所作故；二、大種越所作故；三、資生越所作故。諸根越所作者，謂無處無位眼能聞聲、嗅香、甞味、覺諸觸等，必無是處；能見諸色，斯有是處。如眼根，如是所餘色根一一相望越用差別，如應當知。大種越所作者，謂無處無位地能造作水、火、風用，必無是處；能作地用，斯有是處。如是所餘大種展轉相望越用差別，如應當知。
items.en: What is every distinguishing approach? Relying on the first, the gate of accomplishment, I shall reveal whatever remaining distinguishing characteristic is not subsumed under it. It should be understood that this distinction is, in brief, of three kinds: first, the sense faculties exceeding what they can do; second, the four great elements exceeding what they can do; third, life's sustaining resources exceeding what they can do. Concerning the sense faculties exceeding what they can do: there is no place, no circumstance, in which the eye could hear sound, smell scent, taste flavour, or feel touch — this is never valid; that it sees form is valid. As with the eye faculty, so too, by analogy, should the mutual overreach of each of the remaining faculties be understood. Concerning the four great elements exceeding what they can do: there is no place, no circumstance, in which earth could perform the function of water, fire, or wind — this is never valid; that it performs earth's own function is valid. As with earth, so too, by analogy, should the mutual overreach of the remaining great elements be understood.

items.title: Section: Milking a Cow's Horn, Churning Butter from Water, and Five More Reasons Cause and Effect Cannot Be Faked

items.zh: 資生越所作者，謂無處無位從餘類種餘類芽生，必無是處；唯自種類，斯有是處。無處無位搆牛角等而出於乳，必無是處；搆彼乳房，斯有是處。無處無位鑽搖水瓶而出生酥，必無是處；鑽搖於酪，斯有是處。無處無位壓沙出油，必無是處；壓苣蕂等，斯有是處。無處無位鑽濕木等而出於火，必無是處；鑽於乾木，斯有是處。如是等類，應當觀察初處非處門差別之相。云何第二處非處門差別？謂無處無位光明、黑闇一時合會，無有是處；若有一處無第二生，斯有是處。
items.en: Concerning life's sustaining resources exceeding what they can do: there is no place, no circumstance, in which a sprout of one kind could arise from a seed of a different kind — this is never valid; only a seed's own kind is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which squeezing a cow's horn could yield milk — this is never valid; squeezing the udder is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which churning a water-jar could yield cream — this is never valid; churning yogurt is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which pressing sand could yield oil — this is never valid; pressing sesame and the like is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which drilling damp wood could yield fire — this is never valid; drilling dry wood is valid. Cases such as these should be observed as illustrating the first gate's own distinguishing characteristic. What distinguishes the second gate of the valid and the invalid? There is no place, no circumstance, in which light and darkness could combine together at one time — this is not valid; that wherever one is present the other does not arise is valid.

items.title: Section: Closing the Combination Gate — Minds That Cannot Overlap, and Fortunes That Cannot Mix

items.zh: 無處無位麁分水火一時合會，無有是處；隨有一種，斯有是處。無處無位二麁色聚同據一處，無有是處；若一極微，斯有是處。無處無位同一種類二心心法俱時合會，無有是處；一一而生，斯有是處。無處無位同一種類若善不善、若善無記不善無記、若苦若樂俱時合會，無有是處；隨有一種，斯有是處。無處無位愛非愛果俱時合會，無有是處；若隨有一，斯有是處。如是等類，應當觀察第二處非處門差別之相。
items.en: There is no place, no circumstance, in which coarse water and fire could combine together at one time — this is not valid; that only one of them is present is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which two coarse material aggregates could occupy the same location — this is not valid; that a single subtle particle can do so is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which two mental phenomena of the same class could combine together at the same moment — this is not valid; that they arise one at a time is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which wholesome and unwholesome, wholesome and neutral, unwholesome and neutral, or painful and pleasant states of the same class could combine together — this is not valid; that only one such state is present is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which a desired and an undesired result could combine together — this is not valid; that only one is present is valid. Cases such as these should be observed as illustrating the second gate's own distinguishing characteristic.

items.title: Section: Why a Barren Woman Cannot Bear Children, and Why Liberation Cannot Be Attained Without the Proper Provisions

items.zh: 云何第三處非處門差別？謂無處無位石女生兒，無有是處；若非石女，斯有是處。無處無位生半擇迦能生男女，無有是處；若諸丈夫，斯有是處。無處無位盲眼見色、聾耳聞聲、鼻舌壞者嗅香甞味，無有是處；諸根不壞，斯有是處。無處無位未具資糧，於現法中證學無學究竟解脫，無有是處；已具資糧，斯有是處。無處無位未得聖道能證涅槃，及證聲聞、獨覺菩提，若證無上正等菩提，無有是處；已得聖道，斯有是處。
items.en: What distinguishes the third gate of the valid and the invalid? There is no place, no circumstance, in which a barren woman could bear a child — this is not valid; that a woman without such impairment can is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one born without proper male faculties could father sons or daughters — this is not valid; that a properly constituted man can is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which the blind could see form, the deaf could hear sound, or one with destroyed nose or tongue could smell or taste — this is not valid; that one whose faculties are unimpaired can is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one lacking the proper provisions could, in this present life, attain the ultimate liberation of a trainee or an adept beyond training — this is not valid; that one who has assembled the provisions can is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one who has not attained the noble path could realise nirvāṇa, the awakening of a hearer or solitary realiser, or unsurpassed perfect awakening — this is not valid; that one who has attained the noble path can is valid.

items.title: Section: King Bimbisāra's Fatal Craving for Heavenly Food, and Closing the Attainment Gate

items.zh: 無處無位人趣有情以傍生趣草等飲食以充節會，若諸天眾食人飲食，色無色界食諸段食，無有是處；與此相違，斯有是處。無處無位不捨那落迦所有身形而得人身，如是不捨所餘身形而得餘身，無有是處；捨已方得，斯有是處。如是等類，應當觀察第三處非處門差別之相。
items.en: There is no place, no circumstance, in which a human being could nourish the body's limbs with an animal's food such as grass, in which the heavenly multitudes could eat human food, or in which the form and formless realms could take solid food — this is not valid; the opposite of this is valid. There is no place, no circumstance, in which one could obtain a human body without relinquishing whatever body-form belongs to the hells, and likewise for obtaining any other body without relinquishing whatever body-form one currently holds — this is not valid; that one obtains a new body only after relinquishing the old is valid. Cases such as these should be observed as illustrating the third gate's own distinguishing characteristic.

blocks.text: Fascicle 57 continues the "skills" (善巧). The fifth is skill in what is possible and impossible: the law that causes give only their fitting results.

The valid is what does not contradict a matter's principle; the invalid, what does. Master Cháng Bǎi: what fully accords with "such a cause brings such a result" is valid. A defiled cause brings a defiled result and a pure cause a pure one.
Accomplishment, combination, attainment, and manifestation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise shows what cannot be done, and so by contrast what can.
Among things that cannot be accomplished: milking a cow's horn, churning butter from water. Master Cháng Bǎi: only one's own kind yields a sprout of that kind.
Two coarse material things cannot occupy one place. Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse clusters have resistance.
Master Cháng Bǎi: without hearing, reflection, and cultivation, without discipline, concentration, and wisdom, one cannot attain the fruit.
One cannot obtain a human body without giving up the hell-form; one gains the new only after relinquishing the old.
"Such a cause, such a result." The Buddha taught the possible and impossible so that effort would be placed where it can actually bear fruit.

quiz.q: What are the valid and the invalid?
options: what yields a result is valid and what does not invalid, accord with principle being no criterion
wholesome phenomena are valid; evil ones invalid
form is valid; the formless invalid
no contradiction with a matter's principle is valid; contradiction is invalid
quiz.why: The treatise defines the valid as no contradiction with a matter's principle, and the invalid as contradiction. Master Cháng Bǎi: what fully accords with the principle that such a cause brings such a result is valid; what contradicts cause and effect, cause and result not matching, is invalid. The English "valid" leans towards logic, where the lecture stresses cause and effect.

quiz.q: The English has "correct wisdom and skilful means" for 正方便智. How does the lecture read this?
options: two things, wisdom being supramundane and means worldly, so the English is right to separate them, as the lecture does
one of the Buddha's ten powers, unrelated to ordinary beings
it is one wisdom from correctly reflecting on cause and result; the English divides it into wisdom and means
a means of giving, unrelated to wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a defiled cause brings a defiled result and a pure cause a pure result, and wisdom obtained by correctly reflecting on this is what is meant. So 正方便智 is a single wisdom concerning means. The English "correct wisdom and skilful means" makes two things, and "skilful means" carries a sense not intended here.

quiz.q: Through which four gates did the Buddha teach the valid and invalid?
options: suffering, origin, cessation, and the path, all valid and invalid lying within the four truths
the three realms and the supramundane
accomplishment, combination, attainment, and active manifestation
seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing
quiz.why: The treatise names the gates of accomplishment, combination, attainment, and active manifestation. Master Cháng Bǎi: summarised in four, they cover the valid, which accords with cause and result, and the invalid. Note the English has both "approaches" and "gates" for 門 in one passage.

quiz.q: The gate of accomplishment says the eye cannot hear. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say is the purpose of this form of statement?
options: first showing what cannot be accomplished, and denying the unreasonable, what remains is reasonable
the eye is inferior and needs the ear, so practice must use all six together, this being the point
powers allow the faculties to interchange
it shows faculties can share functions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the treatise first shows what cannot be accomplished, and so by contrast what can; invalid examples confirm the valid; putting forward and denying the unreasonable leaves what is reasonable. The English "no place, no circumstance" translates 無處無位; the lecture reads 位 as time, covering all space and time.

quiz.q: What examples does the gate of combination give, and why can two coarse clusters not share a place while a particle can?
options: light and dark, water and fire do not combine; coarse clusters obstruct, while a particle, the smallest unit, intermixes with coarse form
light and dark can combine at dusk, and water and fire make steam, so all these are valid
coarse clusters can share a place, particles cannot
no form can share a place, not even particles
quiz.why: The treatise says two coarse material aggregates cannot occupy one place, while a single particle can. Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse clusters have resistance, and so two cannot occupy one place; the particle, the smallest unit of form, intermixes with coarse form without separation. The same gate lists light and dark, and coarse water and fire.

quiz.q: What examples are given of life's resources exceeding what they can do?
options: the eye hearing, the ear seeing, the nose tasting, and so on, all overreach of faculties, under the gate of resources
light and dark together, water and fire together
a sprout from another kind's seed, milk from a horn, cream from a water-jar, oil from sand, fire from damp wood
a barren woman bearing, the blind seeing
quiz.why: The treatise lists these among things that cannot be accomplished. Master Cháng Bǎi: only one's own kind yields a sprout of that kind; as a seed gives its sprout, such a cause gives such a result, and only where cause and result match is it reasonable. The same principle is meant to apply to karma.

quiz.q: The English has "the ultimate liberation of a trainee or an adept beyond training." What is the problem?
options: in the Chinese trainees and adepts are equally final, trainees having attained everything an adept has, so the English is exact and nothing in the lecture separates them
the problem is "provisions," 資糧 not being accumulated conditions
the Chinese says one attains without provisions
final liberation belongs only to adepts; the English makes trainees' final too; the lecture says one attains only with provisions complete
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: without the provisions, with hearing, reflection, and cultivation, discipline, concentration, and wisdom unachieved, one cannot attain the fruit. The Chinese names attainments of trainees and adepts, and "final" fits only the adept. The English attaches "ultimate" to both, which would give a trainee what a trainee by definition lacks.

quiz.q: Humans do not eat fodder and gods not human food. What of the form realm, and what is needed to gain a human body, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: form-realm gods eat too, only more finely; a hell-being may gain a human body without leaving the old one
form-realm gods take solid food, though not human food
the hell-form is never given up
the form realm lacks smell, taste, and their consciousnesses, needing no solid food; the hell-form must be given up before a human body
quiz.why: The treatise says one cannot obtain a human body without relinquishing the hell-form; one gains the new only after relinquishing the old. Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm gods lack the four elements of smell, taste, and nose- and tongue-consciousness, and need no solid food. The English "nourish the body's limbs" for 節會 is a good choice.
